coaching.headline: The duo lane got fucking farmed: Kira and Steel took nine of the eleven team deaths, and not one fight was won.

flags.text: Zinx and Eden scored eight of the enemy's eleven kills, every one on Kira or Steel.
The enemy took the opening kill in four of five fights, every time on Steel.
The team took six of the first eight river buffs; the enemy took all six after that.
Bayle's rotation kill on Zinx answered Kira's death in the duo lane, and Bayle never died.

focus.title: Fix the duo before contesting river
focus.action: When the duo keeps dying, send the jungler or the offlaner there before contesting the next river buff, and have Kira and Steel give up the wave until help arrives.

3.call: Zinx killed Steel, Kira killed Zinx and Eden killed Kira on the duo side; Grux killed The Fey in mid. Two separate plays, both lost, and the team took a river buff in the same window.

6.5.call: Zinx killed Steel and Eden killed Kira on the duo side, with no enemy deaths. The team took a river buff in the same window.

8.3.call: Kira killed Eden, Zinx killed Kira and Grux killed The Fey within seconds, a fight lost one kill to two, while the team took the only Fangtooth of the game.

11.8.call: Gideon killed Steel, Eden killed Kira, Kira killed Grux and Bayle killed Zinx on the duo side, an even trade at two kills each. The enemy took a river buff in the same window.

14.8.call: Zinx killed Steel and Kira with no enemy deaths, the last kills of the game, and the enemy took two river buffs in the same window.

5c8cbd99-c52b-428d-87cc-fcfca4d654a1: Hero damage ran 324 per minute against a norm of 817, while Gideon, the mid opponent, dealt the most hero damage in the game.
Both deaths came to Grux, fewer than the norm. Next game, chain Harvest Nettles on the same hero: each repeat hit within eight seconds stacks more damage.
945f7a88-d3eb-40fc-a02a-2449feddf549: Zero deaths against a norm above four, the only laner who never died.
Hero damage ran 361 per minute against a norm of 606; Serath, the lane opponent, finished without a kill or death. When the offlane is quiet, repeat the duo rotation.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Zero deaths and 6290 objective damage, the most in the game, while the team took the game's only Fangtooth.
Hero damage ran 155 per minute against a norm of 521, with two assists in five team kills.
Two wards placed against a norm of 6.9, but two enemy wards cleared, the most in the game. If wards were equipped, cover the duo-side river.
9df9186c-d73f-4f00-a546-daa15a642f41: Five deaths, the most in the game: three to Eden, two to Zinx. Favored on paper against Eden, but Eden won the kills three to one.
Still the team's sharpest weapon: three of the five team kills, one each on Zinx, Eden and Grux, and the most hero damage on the team.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: A hand in two of the five team kills and the most damage mitigated on the team, but four deaths, three to Zinx, including first blood.
Three wards placed against a norm of six, and none cleared. If a sentry was equipped, sweep the duo-side river before trading with Zinx and Eden.

matchup: Kira died three times to Eden and twice to Zinx, and killed each once.
Eden's melee stance heals off hero damage, and Eden's Vanquisher executes heroes left at very low health.
Zinx's Neural Regenesis revives an ally on lethal damage, so a kill on Eden can be undone.
build: Nothing in the build, crest included, carries armor or health, against Eden's physical damage.
Ashbringer's basic attacks cut non-ultimate cooldowns, more on critical strikes, so Shadow Glide returns sooner.
Lightning Hawk builds charge while moving or attacking, and the charged basic attack adds damage and a slow.
eternal: Weald fires true-damage missiles when Kira damages a hero below a health threshold, a finisher on low targets.
Wind-Rider adds attack speed after a dash, which Shadow Glide supplies; Dryad's Boon trims basic ability cooldowns on hit.
Natural Resistance is the first-minor alternative into Zinx's Ricochet stun: a cleanse at low health, giving up Dryad's Boon.
augment: Lenore makes Shadow Glide refresh Nevermore, the Raven shot that hits for a share of the target's current health.
Bringer Of Mercy is the field's most-run Kira augment: Mercy hits cut current cooldowns, giving up the Raven refresh.
crest: Assassin Crest is the base tier: health back on ability hits and unit kills, evolving after enough healing and a base visit.
Pacifier, the field's usual Kira crest, adds a dash beside Shadow Glide, plus lifesteal.
improvement: The winning core is Solaris, Ashbringer and Imperator; Ashbringer is in, and Lightning Hawk sits outside the core.
Solaris next adds an empowered basic attack after each ability cast that heals off the damage dealt.
If Eden keeps winning trades, compare Draconum: physical armor and takedown healing, giving up the critical chance Solaris or Imperator adds.

matchup: Duo was Steel and Kira against Zinx and Eden; Zinx killed Steel three times, first blood included.
Zinx's Ricochet stuns the first enemy hit and bounces to more targets, and Bad Medicine slows twice in a pool.
Gideon took the other Steel death; Gideon's Black Hole pulls nearby enemies in while channeling.
build: Xenia shields an ally hero standing close by and adds both armors, health and ability haste.
Xenia's armor also feeds Heavy Metal's bonus damage and Cybernetic Shell's hybrid armor scaling.
eternal: Krix adds maximum health that grows with level; Regenerative Tissue regenerates after a stretch without hero damage.
Cannibalism paid twice: two takedowns, two permanent health stacks.
Festering Wounds is the first-minor alternative: Steel's stuns would cut healing on Eden, giving up the regeneration.
augment: Heavy Metal adds magical damage to heavy punches and Shield Bash, scaling with Steel's total armor; the field's most-run pick.
Bulldozer is the alternative: damage reduction during Bull Rush, giving up the armor-scaled damage.
crest: Sanctification's Safeguard shields Steel and nearby heroes and grants tenacity while the shield holds, against Zinx's stuns.
Sanctification raises the ward cap, a bonus that pays only when wards keep going down; three went down all game.
improvement: The winning core is Xenia, Dynamo and Gaia Greaves; Xenia was the one finished.
Dynamo next makes each immobilized enemy take more damage, a payoff for the Shield Bash and Shield Slam stuns.

matchup: Grux was the jungle opponent: two kills, both on The Fey, one death to Kira, and the most damage taken.
Grux's Double Pain heals per hero hit, and Grux had the most healing in the game.
Eden, Serath and Grux deal physical damage, and neither Spirit Of Amir nor Warlock Crest carries armor.
build: Spirit Of Amir gives magical lifesteal inside the jungle, magical power outside the jungle, and more ability damage to monsters.
The monster damage suits the most objective damage in the game; against Eden's physical damage the item adds health but no armor.
eternal: Lotus grants a small random bonus on a timer and on each takedown; two takedowns fed Lotus.
Flawless heals Aurora and nearby allies on ability hits against heroes; Fragrance adds magical damage to nearby heroes.
Krix with Predator is the field's most-run Aurora jungle Eternal: more health, giving up Flawless's group healing.
augment: Glacial Thorns makes Glacial Charge spawn crystals that damage and briefly root, the field's most-run pick.
Hypothermia is the alternative into Grux: Boreal Sweep shreds both armors and slows attack speed, giving up that root.
crest: Warlock Crest is the base tier: health back on ability damage and unit kills, evolving after enough healing and a base visit.
Tempest is the field's most-run Aurora jungle crest: a burn on nearby heroes that heals off the damage.
improvement: The winning core is Spirit Of Amir, Magnify and Spectral Schematics; Spirit Of Amir was the one finished.
If Eden or Grux keep landing hits, compare Golem's Gift next: physical armor and magical power, giving up Magnify's health and omnivamp.

matchup: Serath was the lane opponent; Bayle out-damaged Serath, 5420 hero damage to 3902.
Serath's Heaven's Fury grants invulnerability and control immunity while vanished, so hold Cursed Edge's stun until Serath reappears.
Skull Crusher shreds the armor of marked enemies, useful against Grux, the game's sturdiest frontline.
build: Manta Scythe adds physical power, penetration, attack speed and lifesteal, plus bonus damage to minions and small monsters.
Divide & Conquer adds damage against a target with no nearby ally, so isolated targets pay.
Goliath Crest's small armor is the only armor in the build, against three physical damage dealers.
eternal: Nihil's Doom stacks power and both armors while Bayle keeps damaging heroes; takedowns and level-ups raise the gains permanently.
From the Abyss regenerates health in hero combat or out of enemy vision; Adaptive Plating adds armor matching damage taken.
Thraex with Alpha's Court and Ferocity is the field's most-run Bayle offlane setup, trading Nihil's armor for solo damage and attack speed.
augment: Frenzied Fighter keeps Berserk on with no cooldown while under the health threshold, the field's most-run pick.
Betrayer's Reqiuem is the alternative for grouped fights: Kingslayer uppercuts everyone around the target, giving up endless Berserk.
crest: Goliath Crest is the base tier: health back on taking damage or killing units, evolving after enough healing and a base visit.
Judgement is the field's most-run Bayle offlane crest: an area hit that heals per hero struck.
improvement: The winning core is Tainted Blade, Rapture and Cursed Scroll; Bayle finished none of the three.
Tainted Blade next cuts healing on every physical hit, against Grux's Double Pain and Zinx's Infuse on Eden.
Cursed Scroll adds both armors and health regeneration, the core's answer to three physical damage dealers.

matchup: Gideon was the mid opponent: 9963 hero damage to The Fey's 4867, and The Fey killed Gideon once.
Gideon's Black Hole pulls nearby enemies while channeling, and Torn Space opens a portal allies can follow through.
Grux killed The Fey twice; Smash 'n Grab pulls and stuns, and Stampede drags heroes along the dash.
build: Combustion adds magical power, penetration and mana, and Pyro bursts the target and nearby enemies on ability damage.
Pyromaniac shortens Pyro's cooldown on hero damage, so Combustion pays most when abilities keep landing on heroes.
eternal: Aion turns spell damage on heroes into gold, so hero damage under half the norm meant less Aion gold.
Philosopher drips passive gold; Arcane Resonance speeds basic ability cooldowns and Philosopher with mana regeneration.
Bottomless Vial is the field's most-run Aion first minor: river buffs refill a potion and add magical power, giving up Philosopher.
augment: Wild Growth extends Bramble Patch's range, the field's most-run pick for the slow zone.
Natural Infusion is the alternative for long trades with Gideon: Harvest Nettles hits on heroes stack ability haste, giving up range.
crest: Epoch's Stasis Device puts The Fey in stasis briefly; Epoch is the field's most-run The Fey mid crest.
Soulbearer is the alternative: a shield, magical lifesteal and movement speed, giving up the stasis.
improvement: The winning core is Combustion, Wraith Leggings and Megacosm; Combustion was the one finished.
Wraith Leggings next adds magical power, penetration and bonus ability damage on low-health heroes, the core path to closing the damage gap.
Two deaths, fewer than the norm, so no defensive swap is called for; the build path is a sound keep.

threats: Chain-CC risk (1 hard-CC abilities, ~0.5s of lockdown): Grux Crush (knockup 0.5s). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Dive threat on our backline: Serath. Assign peel for the carry and ward the flanks.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Bayle Kingslayer (knockback). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Bramble Patch slow → Harvest Nettles stacks → Untamed Growth DoT → Fly Trap pull ult
ourKits.winCondition: Fly Trap a clumped team and detonate AoE on the pull
ourKits.passive: takedowns spawn growths + grant move speed
ourKits.playWith: engage that clumps for her Fly Trap
ourKits.playAgainst: spread out vs the pull; she's squishy — dive her

ourKits.combo: Skull Crusher gap-close → Dire Howl slow → Cursed Edge → Kingslayer knockback dash, Berserk at low HP
ourKits.winCondition: engage, drop low into Berserk and out-brawl
ourKits.playWith: follow-up while he commits the dive
ourKits.playAgainst: his Berserk rewards low HP — burst him fully or disengage; anti-heal helps

ourKits.combo: Boreal Sweep slow → Hoarfrost root → Glacial Charge engage → Cryoseism stun ult
ourKits.winCondition: chain frost CC (slow→root→stun) to lock the fight down
ourKits.playWith: burst that converts her long CC chain into kills
ourKits.playAgainst: she's a CC battery — cleanse/QSS the Cryoseism stun; spread to avoid the chain

ourKits.combo: Mercy poke → stack Vengeance → Shadow Glide reposition → Purge ult
ourKits.winCondition: stack Vengeance and shred with the channeled Purge
ourKits.playWith: peel so she can channel Purge safely
ourKits.playAgainst: interrupt/CC her during Purge; punish her short dash cooldown

ourKits.combo: Bull Rush knockback → Force Shield wall → Shield Slam knockup+stun ult, Shield Bash %hp
ourKits.winCondition: peel the carry with walls/knockups or engage with Shield Slam
ourKits.playWith: a carry he can wall for and peel
ourKits.playAgainst: his Force Shield blocks projectiles — reposition around it; bait Shield Slam

enemyKits.combo: Ricochet stun → Bad Medicine zone → Infuse heal an ally → Neural Regenesis revive
enemyKits.winCondition: keep an ally alive with Infuse + the revive ult and poke with Ricochet
enemyKits.playWith: a carry she can pocket-heal and revive
enemyKits.playAgainst: she can't heal herself — dive HER; bait the revive before committing

enemyKits.combo: stance-swap with Zero Shift → Tachyon Lance (ranged) or melee chain → Limit Break on Overheat
enemyKits.winCondition: build Heat and burst with Limit Break, flexing range and melee
enemyKits.passive: damage builds Heat → Overheat unlocks Limit Break
enemyKits.playWith: peel that lets her ramp Heat safely
enemyKits.playAgainst: pressure her before Overheat; CC during the melee stance

enemyKits.combo: Ascend dive → Heaven's Fury multi-strike → Chastise slow → Heresy form ult, resets on takedowns
enemyKits.winCondition: dive the backline and snowball Heresy resets
enemyKits.playWith: a frontline that creates her dive angle
enemyKits.playAgainst: peel the backline — deny the first kill and her resets dry up

enemyKits.combo: Void Breach slow → Cosmic Rift → Black Hole on the grouped enemies
enemyKits.winCondition: land Black Hole / Cosmic Rift on a clumped team for AoE burst
enemyKits.passive: an ability-empowered basic tethers a target for bonus damage
enemyKits.playWith: hard engage that clumps enemies into his Black Hole
enemyKits.playAgainst: immobile with long cooldowns — dodge the skillshots and dive him once Black Hole is down

enemyKits.combo: Smash 'n Grab pull → Crush knockup → Warlord's Challenge stun → bleed-stacked basics
enemyKits.winCondition: land the pull→knockup chain to lock a target while bleed and AS shred them
enemyKits.passive: basics stack a bleed for sustained damage
enemyKits.playWith: follow-up burst inside his knockup/stun window
enemyKits.playAgainst: telegraphed engage — bait Crush/Pull, then punish; kite his slow start
